transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Could you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, yeah… I came in because I’ve been trying to kind of clean up my image and my routine, mostly for this arts board stuff I’m involved with, and I thought that would make me feel more together, but it’s sort of done the opposite.

I’m still doing the basics, like I’m not completely falling apart or anything, but I’ve been more tense and kind of down than I expected. And then I keep dropping these little things I normally care about—like fair planning notes, or design drafts I was supposed to work on—and then I feel guilty about it and end up canceling plans instead of just catching up. It’s frustrating because it’s not even huge things, but it keeps happening.
Have you noticed that you’re not enjoying things that you usually like to do, like working on your art or planning events?

Yeah, kind of. I mean, I still care about the art stuff and the fair planning, it’s not like I suddenly hate it. But since I started trying to make myself look more put-together for the arts board, everything around it feels heavier.

Like, I’ll have design drafts I meant to work on, or notes for the fair, and then I just… don’t do them, or I put them off. And then I feel guilty, so instead of catching up or going to meet people, I’ll cancel plans. Which is dumb, because those are usually the things I like, you know? It’s just been making me more tense and down than I expected.
Can you describe how you feel when you're working on your art or planning events now compared to before you started feeling this way?

Before, working on art or event stuff felt kind of energizing, like it gave me something to focus on. Now it still matters to me, but it feels heavier. Like I’ll sit down with design drafts or fair planning notes and suddenly I’m thinking about whether I seem organized enough for the arts board, or if I’m messing up some image I’m supposed to have.

And then I get tense, and if I don’t get it done I feel guilty, and instead of just picking it back up later I’ll cancel plans or avoid people. It’s weird because I’m still doing the basic day-to-day things, but these little things I normally care about keep slipping.
How long have you been feeling this way, and would you say your mood has been consistently low during this time?

Um… I think it’s been about two months? It kind of started when I decided I needed to overhaul my routine and how I present myself, like trying to seem more polished for the arts board. At first I thought it was just the usual stress of changing habits, but it’s sort of stayed around.

And the mood… I don’t know if I’d say low every single minute, but it’s been there a lot of the time since then, like this background heaviness.
Have you noticed any trouble concentrating or making decisions lately, especially when working on your art or planning events?

Yeah… I mean, kind of. Like with the design drafts or the fair planning notes, I’ll sit down and I know what I’m supposed to do, but then I get stuck thinking about whether I’m seeming put-together enough for the arts board, and suddenly the actual task feels way bigger than it is.

It’s not like I can’t function at all — I’m still doing the basic stuff. But these smaller things I normally care about keep slipping, and then I feel guilty, and instead of catching up I’ll cancel plans or avoid dealing with it. It’s just been more tense and heavy than I expected since I tried to clean up my image and routine.
Have you been feeling more tired or lacking energy more often than usual, even when you’re not physically exhausted?

I’m not totally sure. I wouldn’t say I’m physically exhausted all the time or anything like that. Sometimes I feel kind of drained when I’m staring at what I need to do, but I don’t know if that’s “low energy” exactly or just me getting in my head.

Like, I’ll sit there with my sketchbook open and then remember I still haven’t organized my supplies — which, honestly, I’ve been meaning to do for weeks because they’re all in this one bin from when I moved things around — and then I kind of lose momentum. But I haven’t really been tracking whether I’m more tired than usual.
Have you found that you’re not really interested in your art or event planning anymore, even when you have the time or opportunity to do it?

I don’t think it’s that I don’t care about it anymore, exactly. Like, I still care about the art and the fair stuff — maybe too much, honestly — but since I tried to clean up my image and routine for the arts board, I’ve just been more tense and kind of down than I expected.

So I’ll have time to work on design drafts or fair planning notes, and instead of doing them I’ll get stuck, or drop some little thing I normally would’ve handled. Then I feel guilty about it, and sometimes I cancel plans instead of catching up. It’s frustrating because it’s not like I’ve stopped wanting to do it, I’m still doing the basics, but it feels harder to stay on top of the parts I used to be more excited about.
Have you noticed that you’re not getting as much enjoyment or satisfaction from your art or event planning as you used to, even when you do manage to work on them?

Yeah… I guess not as much, but it’s weird because I still do care about it. Like, if I’m working on a design draft, part of me still likes the idea of it, but then I start thinking about how it’s going to look to the arts board, or whether I seem like I have everything together, and it kind of sucks the satisfaction out of it.

And the fair planning notes — I’ll do some of them, but then I’ll notice I missed some small thing I normally would’ve handled, and I get guilty instead of feeling accomplished. Then I’ll end up canceling plans or putting off catching up, which makes it worse. So it’s not that I’ve stopped enjoying art completely, it’s more like since I tried to clean up my image and routine, everything around it feels tense and heavier than it used to.
Have you noticed that you’ve been moving more slowly than usual, or fidgety and restless lately, even when you’re not trying to be?

Um… I don’t think I’ve really noticed that. Like, I’m not sure I would catch myself moving slower unless someone pointed it out.

Sometimes I’ll get up to do something and then end up sort of wandering around my room because I see, like, a pile of receipts or an art supply I forgot to put away, and then I’m doing three little things instead of the one thing I meant to do. But I don’t know if that’s fidgety, exactly, or just me being distracted.

I haven’t had anyone tell me I seem slowed down or restless, though. At least not that I can think of.
Have you been feeling like you're not good enough or that you're failing at things, especially related to how you're presenting yourself to the arts board?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say I think I’m failing at everything, but with the arts board stuff, yeah, it kind of gets in my head.

Like, I came in because once I started trying to clean up my image and my routine for that, I got way more tense and down than I expected. I’m still doing the basic things, it’s not like I’ve totally fallen apart, but I keep dropping these little things I normally care about — fair planning notes, design draft details, stuff like that — and then I feel really guilty.

And then instead of just catching up, I’ll cancel plans or avoid dealing with it for a bit, which makes me feel even more like I’m not presenting myself the way I should. It’s… frustrating.
Have you felt like nothing really interests you or gives you pleasure anymore, even things you usually like doing outside of the arts board stuff?

I don’t know if I’d say nothing interests me anymore. That sounds… bigger than what I mean, I think.

Like, I still like things outside of all that, or at least I think I do. Sometimes I’ll start doing something random, like looking at little apartment decor ideas or watching someone paint online, and then somehow I’m thinking about whether my own workspace looks messy, which is not really the point. Sorry, that’s kind of a side thing.

But no, I haven’t really noticed that absolutely nothing gives me pleasure. It’s more hard for me to separate what I actually enjoy from all the pressure around looking like I’m doing okay.
Have you found yourself losing interest in almost all activities, even the ones you usually enjoy outside of your art and the fair planning?

I’m not sure it’s almost all activities, no. I mean… I still get pulled into things, like if I see a video about someone making tiny ceramics or reorganizing a shelf in a really satisfying way, I’ll watch it longer than I meant to.

But then I start thinking, “Oh, my shelves look kind of chaotic,” and then it turns into this whole thing in my head instead of just enjoying it. So I guess I’m not sure if that counts as losing interest, or just not being able to stay with the enjoyment without it turning into… I don’t know, another comparison thing.

I haven’t noticed that everything feels flat, though.
Have you felt like you don’t really care about doing most of the things you used to enjoy, even outside of your art and the fair planning?

I don’t think it’s most things, exactly. Or… I’m not sure. I still care about stuff in flashes, like if a friend sends me a weird thrifted lamp or some cute room setup, I’ll have opinions immediately.

But then I start drifting into, like, “Should I be making my place look more pulled together?” And that’s not really the same as not caring, I guess. It just gets tangled up. So I wouldn’t say I don’t care about things I used to enjoy… I just don’t always stay with them in a normal, easy way.
Have you felt like you’ve lost interest in most of the things you used to enjoy, even outside of your art and the fair planning, like hobbies or time with friends?

I don’t think I’ve lost interest in most things, no. I mean, I’ve been less… I don’t know, easygoing about them, maybe.

Like with friends, if someone asks me to hang out, I might overthink it for a while, but once I’m actually there I can still enjoy parts of it. And hobbies are kind of the same — I’ll start something and then get distracted by whether I’m doing it “right,” which is annoying, because even making a playlist turns into this whole weird decision process sometimes.

But I wouldn’t say I just don’t care about any of it anymore. It’s more like my attention keeps getting hijacked.
Would you say that you’ve lost interest in most of the things you used to enjoy, even the small ones, like hobbies, time with friends, or even things around your home?

I’m still not sure I’d call it “lost interest in most things.” Like, the small home stuff is actually where I can get weirdly interested — I’ll notice a corner looks messy and suddenly I’m looking at baskets online for 40 minutes, and then I’m not even sure if I wanted baskets or if I just got distracted.

With friends, too, it’s not like I don’t want to see them. I can still have a good time once I’m there. I guess it just takes more mental… sorting? But no, I haven’t really noticed that most things I used to enjoy feel totally uninteresting.

Have you noticed that your thoughts are slowing down or that you're physically moving more slowly than usual, or on the flip side, that you're more restless or fidgety than before, even when you're not trying to be?

I don’t think I’ve noticed that, not in a clear way. Like, I fidget sometimes, but I’ve always kind of done that — tapping my foot or messing with a sleeve or whatever.

The “thoughts slowing down” thing is harder for me to tell, because sometimes I’ll sit there deciding between two stupidly similar things, like which mug to use, and it feels like my brain is being dramatic. But I don’t know if that’s slowed down exactly. Physically, I don’t think anyone would say I’m moving weirdly slow or anything. Restless maybe here and there, but not in a way that feels new enough that I’d be like, “Oh, that’s a symptom.”
Have you felt like nothing you do brings you any real pleasure or satisfaction most of the time, even things you normally enjoy?

I don’t think it’s like nothing brings me pleasure, no. I mean, “real satisfaction” is a hard phrase because sometimes I’ll enjoy something and then immediately start picking it apart, like, was that actually relaxing or did I just spend an hour arranging things on my phone?

But I still get enjoyment from things. Like if I’m with a friend and we end up laughing about something dumb, that still feels good. Or if something at home looks nicer after I fuss with it, I can feel satisfied for a bit. It just doesn’t always stay simple in my head, if that makes sense.
Would you say that you’ve lost interest in most of your usual activities, even the ones you used to enjoy the most, like your art, time with friends, or hobbies around home?

I’m not sure I’d say I’ve lost interest in most of them. Like with art, sometimes I’ll avoid starting because it feels like this whole thing, and then I end up reorganizing my pens or watching a video about someone else’s sketchbook instead, which is not really the same as doing it.

But when I actually sit down with it, I can still get into it sometimes. Same with friends — I might drag my feet getting there, but then I’m usually glad I went. And home stuff, honestly, I still get pulled into that pretty easily. So… no, I don’t think it’s a big loss of interest, more like I’m a little scattered about starting things.
Would you say that most of the time, even when things are going fine, you still feel down or low in mood?

Most of the time… I don’t know if I’d say even when things are going fine, exactly. It’s more like since I tried to clean up my whole image and routine for the arts board stuff, I’ve been more tense and kind of down than I expected.

Like, I’m still doing the basics. I’m getting through the day. But then I drop these little things I normally care about — fair planning notes, or design drafts, stuff like that — and then I feel guilty, and instead of just catching up I’ll cancel plans. Which sounds silly when I say it, because it’s not like the world ends if a draft is late, but it kind of snowballs in my head. So… not constantly low for no reason, but I have been lower than usual around all of that.
Would you say that your mood has been low or down most days, even when nothing particularly bad is happening, and that this has affected how you function in your daily life?

Yeah… I mean, I’m still functioning, like I’m not just staying in bed or missing basic errands. I can still get groceries and show up to things I really have to show up for.

But it has affected me in the areas people usually rely on me for, which is the part that makes me feel bad. Like with the fair planning stuff, or design follow-through, I’ve been… less dependable than I usually am. I’ll tell myself I’m going to send the notes or finish a draft, and then I get weirdly stuck, and then I’m late or I have to apologize. And then I start thinking about how everyone probably sees me as flaky, which is ironic because I used to be the person who cared too much about those details.

So, most days maybe not in this dramatic way, but yes, it’s been enough that I’m not doing as well in the volunteer and creative things people count on me for.

I don’t know if I’d say nothing interests me anymore. That sounds… bigger than what I mean, I think.

Like, I still like things outside of all that, or at least I think I do. Sometimes I’ll start doing something random, like looking at little apartment decor ideas or watching someone paint online, and then somehow I’m thinking about whether my own workspace looks messy, which is not really the point. Sorry, that’s kind of a side thing.

But no, I haven’t really noticed that absolutely nothing gives me pleasure. It’s more hard for me to separate what I actually enjoy from all the pressure around looking like I’m doing okay.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a significant loss of interest or pleasure in most activities, which would support a diagnosis of Major Depressive Disorder (F32.9 or F33.0).
doctor.question: Have you found yourself losing interest in almost all activities, even the ones you usually enjoy outside of your art and the fair planning?

target_item.reason: The question is asking about loss of interest or pleasure in almost all activities, which is not covered by the provided Adjustment Disorder symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure it’s almost all activities, no. I mean… I still get pulled into things, like if I see a video about someone making tiny ceramics or reorganizing a shelf in a really satisfying way, I’ll watch it longer than I meant to.

But then I start thinking, “Oh, my shelves look kind of chaotic,” and then it turns into this whole thing in my head instead of just enjoying it. So I guess I’m not sure if that counts as losing interest, or just not being able to stay with the enjoyment without it turning into… I don’t know, another comparison thing.

I haven’t noticed that everything feels flat, though.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a significant loss of interest in most activities, which would support a diagnosis of Major Depressive Disorder (F32.9 or F33.0) over Adjustment Disorder (F43.22).
doctor.question: Have you felt like you don’t really care about doing most of the things you used to enjoy, even outside of your art and the fair planning?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about loss of interest or pleasure in most previously enjoyed activities, which is not covered by the adjustment-disorder symptom profile provided.

patient.answer:
I don’t think it’s most things, exactly. Or… I’m not sure. I still care about stuff in flashes, like if a friend sends me a weird thrifted lamp or some cute room setup, I’ll have opinions immediately.

But then I start drifting into, like, “Should I be making my place look more pulled together?” And that’s not really the same as not caring, I guess. It just gets tangled up. So I wouldn’t say I don’t care about things I used to enjoy… I just don’t always stay with them in a normal, easy way.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a significant loss of interest or pleasure in most activities, which would help distinguish between a major depressive episode (F32.9) and persistent mild depression (F33.0).
doctor.question: Have you felt like you’ve lost interest in most of the things you used to enjoy, even outside of your art and the fair planning, like hobbies or time with friends?

target_item.reason: The question is specifically about loss of interest or pleasure in most previously enjoyed activities, including hobbies or friends, which is not directly covered by the provided Adjustment Disorder symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I don’t think I’ve lost interest in most things, no. I mean, I’ve been less… I don’t know, easygoing about them, maybe.

Like with friends, if someone asks me to hang out, I might overthink it for a while, but once I’m actually there I can still enjoy parts of it. And hobbies are kind of the same — I’ll start something and then get distracted by whether I’m doing it “right,” which is annoying, because even making a playlist turns into this whole weird decision process sometimes.

But I wouldn’t say I just don’t care about any of it anymore. It’s more like my attention keeps getting hijacked.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a significant loss of interest in most activities, which would help distinguish between F32.9 (depressive episode, unspecified) and the other candidates.

patient.answer:
I’m still not sure I’d call it “lost interest in most things.” Like, the small home stuff is actually where I can get weirdly interested — I’ll notice a corner looks messy and suddenly I’m looking at baskets online for 40 minutes, and then I’m not even sure if I wanted baskets or if I just got distracted.

With friends, too, it’s not like I don’t want to see them. I can still have a good time once I’m there. I guess it just takes more mental… sorting? But no, I haven’t really noticed that most things I used to enjoy feel totally uninteresting.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences significant psychomotor agitation or retardation nearly every day, as this is a key differentiator between mild (F32.9/F33.0) and more severe forms of depression, and may also help rule out adjustment disorder (F43.22).

patient.answer:
I don’t think I’ve noticed that, not in a clear way. Like, I fidget sometimes, but I’ve always kind of done that — tapping my foot or messing with a sleeve or whatever.

The “thoughts slowing down” thing is harder for me to tell, because sometimes I’ll sit there deciding between two stupidly similar things, like which mug to use, and it feels like my brain is being dramatic. But I don’t know if that’s slowed down exactly. Physically, I don’t think anyone would say I’m moving weirdly slow or anything. Restless maybe here and there, but not in a way that feels new enough that I’d be like, “Oh, that’s a symptom.”

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences a persistent loss of interest or pleasure in most activities, which would help differentiate between F32.9 (depressive episode, unspecified) and other candidates like F33.0 (recurrent depressive disorder) or F43.22 (adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood).
doctor.question: Have you felt like nothing you do brings you any real pleasure or satisfaction most of the time, even things you normally enjoy?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about loss of pleasure or satisfaction most of the time (anhedonia), which is not covered by the provided Adjustment Disorder symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I don’t think it’s like nothing brings me pleasure, no. I mean, “real satisfaction” is a hard phrase because sometimes I’ll enjoy something and then immediately start picking it apart, like, was that actually relaxing or did I just spend an hour arranging things on my phone?

But I still get enjoyment from things. Like if I’m with a friend and we end up laughing about something dumb, that still feels good. Or if something at home looks nicer after I fuss with it, I can feel satisfied for a bit. It just doesn’t always stay simple in my head, if that makes sense.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a significant loss of interest in most activities, which is critical for differentiating between F32.9 (Major Depressive Disorder, single episode) and F33.0 (Major Depressive Disorder, recurrent episode), while also assessing overlap with F43.22 (Adjustment Disorder with Depressed Mood).
doctor.question: Would you say that you’ve lost interest in most of your usual activities, even the ones you used to enjoy the most, like your art, time with friends, or hobbies around home?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking specifically about loss of interest or anhedonia in usual activities, which is not directly covered by the provided adjustment disorder symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure I’d say I’ve lost interest in most of them. Like with art, sometimes I’ll avoid starting because it feels like this whole thing, and then I end up reorganizing my pens or watching a video about someone else’s sketchbook instead, which is not really the same as doing it.

But when I actually sit down with it, I can still get into it sometimes. Same with friends — I might drag my feet getting there, but then I’m usually glad I went. And home stuff, honestly, I still get pulled into that pretty easily. So… no, I don’t think it’s a big loss of interest, more like I’m a little scattered about starting things.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has had a persistent low mood that is characteristic of a depressive episode, as opposed to a stress response.
doctor.question: Would you say that most of the time, even when things are going fine, you still feel down or low in mood?

target_item.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
target_item.manifestation: I came in because since I tried to clean up my image and routine for the arts board stuff, I’ve been more tense and down than I expected, like I’m still doing the basics but I keep dropping little things I normally care about, like fair planning notes or design drafts, and then I feel guilty and cancel plans instead of catching up.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about feeling down or low in mood, which is part of the emotional response described in this stress-related maladaptive response profile.

patient.answer:
Most of the time… I don’t know if I’d say even when things are going fine, exactly. It’s more like since I tried to clean up my whole image and routine for the arts board stuff, I’ve been more tense and kind of down than I expected.

Like, I’m still doing the basics. I’m getting through the day. But then I drop these little things I normally care about — fair planning notes, or design drafts, stuff like that — and then I feel guilty, and instead of just catching up I’ll cancel plans. Which sounds silly when I say it, because it’s not like the world ends if a draft is late, but it kind of snowballs in my head. So… not constantly low for no reason, but I have been lower than usual around all of that.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a persistent low mood that meets criteria for a depressive disorder, distinguishing between major depressive disorder (F32.9) and persistent depressive disorder (F33.0), and assessing functional impairment consistent with adjustment disorder (F43.22).
doctor.question: Would you say that your mood has been low or down most days, even when nothing particularly bad is happening, and that this has affected how you function in your daily life?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I am still getting through basic errands and commitments, but I have been less reliable in the volunteer and creative roles people usually count on me for, like fair planning and design follow-through.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the low/down mood has affected daily functioning, which is most directly covered by the functional impairment item.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I mean, I’m still functioning, like I’m not just staying in bed or missing basic errands. I can still get groceries and show up to things I really have to show up for.

But it has affected me in the areas people usually rely on me for, which is the part that makes me feel bad. Like with the fair planning stuff, or design follow-through, I’ve been… less dependable than I usually am. I’ll tell myself I’m going to send the notes or finish a draft, and then I get weirdly stuck, and then I’m late or I have to apologize. And then I start thinking about how everyone probably sees me as flaky, which is ironic because I used to be the person who cared too much about those details.

So, most days maybe not in this dramatic way, but yes, it’s been enough that I’m not doing as well in the volunteer and creative things people count on me for.
